title: A Harbor for the Summer
premise: Xanthe Iversen ghostwrites memoirs for celebrity chef Marlowe Voss, hiding behind other people's words since a scandal ended his own writing career seven years ago. When a letter he mailed eleven years ago to his first love, ferry captain Emeric Hale, finally surfaces undelivered, Xanthe returns to the island harbor town of Pellwick—only to find Emeric engaged in a fight to save his family's ferry line, and unaware that Xanthe is secretly drafting the memoir that could expose the Voss family's role in the Hales' near-ruin. As summer deepens, Xanthe must choose between finishing the lucrative manuscript that keeps him safe and invisible, or publishing the truth under his own name and losing everything except the one thing he came back for. He chooses truth: the memoir is reworked into an exposé credited to him, Marlowe retaliates but fails, and Xanthe boards the last ferry of the season not to leave, but as its new part-owner beside Emeric.
about_author: Dominic Lockridge is a former maritime archivist who spent a decade cataloguing letters that never reached their recipients before turning to fiction. He writes from a converted pilot house on the northern coast, where he still watches the ferries come in.

chapters.title: The Undelivered
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. In a Manhattan archive, a returned-to-sender letter he wrote at twenty-two surfaces among unclaimed mail, postmarked eleven years ago. His hands shake; the words inside were never meant for anyone else's eyes. Emotional beat: the past knocking politely on a door he bricked over.

chapters.title: Ghostwork
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. He meets Marlowe Voss to sign the contract for her tell-all memoir—his biggest payday since the scandal. The advance would buy real security. He tells himself the letter can wait. Emotional beat: the seductive comfort of being someone else's voice.

chapters.title: Last Ferry Out
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. He takes the late-season crossing to Pellwick, telling himself it's research for a chapter about coastal towns. From the deck he sees Emeric Hale at the helm of the rival ferry, older, broader, unmistakable. Emotional beat: terror disguised as curiosity.

chapters.title: The Man at the Wheel
chapters.summary: Emeric's POV. Emeric notices the stranger asking odd questions at the dock—then recognizes Xanthe and says nothing, just hands him a coffee like no time has passed. That night he rereads his own unsent replies, kept in a tin box. Emotional beat: hope arriving without permission.

chapters.title: Salt and Small Talk
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Xanthe rents a cottage for 'the season' and the two circle each other with careful, wry conversations about tides, engines, and everything they're not saying. Emotional beat: intimacy rebuilding itself out of small safe steps.

chapters.title: What the Harbor Remembers
chapters.summary: Emeric's POV. Emeric shows Xanthe the harbor's decline: the Voss ferry corporation undercutting the family line for years, his father's bankruptcy, his mother's quiet death. Xanthe realizes what Marlowe's memoir will whitewash. Emotional beat: loyalty to a story he hasn't finished being paid to write.

chapters.title: Interviews and Inventions
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Back home between trips, Xanthe interviews Marlowe, who spins the Hales' ruin as 'market forces.' He transcribes her lies in his own beautiful sentences and hates how good he is at it. Emotional beat: complicity settling into the bones.

chapters.title: The Tin Box
chapters.summary: Emeric's POV. A storm strands Xanthe on the island; in Emeric's kitchen, the tin box comes out—eleven years of letters Emeric wrote and never sent after Xanthe vanished following the scandal. Neither sleeps. Emotional beat: grief and tenderness colliding at last.

chapters.title: Almost Honest
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. They fall into something real—mornings on the water, nights talking until dawn—but Xanthe still hides the memoir contract. Emeric, burned once by Xanthe's disappearance, asks nothing and fears everything. Emotional beat: happiness built on a hairline crack.

chapters.title: Marlowe Comes Calling
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Marlowe arrives on the island unannounced, charming the town while privately warning Xanthe that the manuscript is due and that she knows where he's spending his summer. She hints she'll bury the Hale chapter deeper. Emotional beat: the two lives converging, neither survivable alone.

chapters.title: Deadline Weather
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Holed up in the cottage, Xanthe drafts Marlowe's chapters by day and walks the shore by night, unable to finish either life. He drafts a confession email to Emeric eleven times and deletes it eleven times. Emotional beat: the cost of safety itemized.

chapters.title: The Second Letter
chapters.summary: Emeric's POV. Emeric finds the old letter's draft in Xanthe's cottage trash—proof Xanthe knew about the undelivered letter for weeks and said nothing. Old wounds reopen: the boy who left, the man who lies by omission. Emotional beat: betrayal wearing love's face.

chapters.title: Cold Crossing
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. A frozen week of silence. Emeric throws himself into a desperate bid to win the harbor contract; Xanthe finishes Marlowe's manuscript and submits it, feeling the door close behind him. Emotional beat: both men choosing their armor.

chapters.title: What Marlowe Knew
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Fact-checking the final manuscript, Xanthe uncovers documents proving Marlowe's father deliberately sabotaged the Hale ferry line—a crime the memoir was designed to bury. He holds the proof that could save Emeric or end his career. Emotional beat: the exact weight of a choice.

chapters.title: Confession at Low Tide
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Xanthe tells Emeric everything—the ghostwriting, the letter, the sabotage evidence, all of it—and offers no excuses. Emeric doesn't forgive him, but he doesn't turn him away either. Emotional beat: truth as the only bridge left standing.

chapters.title: The Public Reading
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Marlowe launches her memoir tour with a stop in Pellwick, reading flattering falsehoods to the town. Emeric attends, jaw set; Xanthe stands in the back, watching his own sentences performed as someone else's armor. Emotional beat: shame made public, resolve made private.

chapters.title: Burning the Manuscript
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Xanthe confronts Marlowe, tears up the remaining payments, and announces he's publishing the sabotage evidence under his own name, scandal be damned. She threatens litigation and blacklisting; he walks out lighter than he's felt in seven years. Emotional beat: invisibility voluntarily surrendered.

chapters.title: Storm Season
chapters.summary: Emeric's POV. Marlowe's lawyers move to seize the Hale dock over an old debt just as a storm cripples the island's power. Emeric runs emergency crossings through dangerous water; Xanthe shows up unasked, working the lines beside him. Emotional beat: trust rebuilt in rope burns and shared labor.

chapters.title: Bylines and Lifelines
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Xanthe publishes the exposé under his own byline; the scandal of Marlowe's buried crime eclipses his old disgrace overnight. Publishers call; so does Marlowe, once, furious, then not at all. Emotional beat: a name reclaimed at last.

chapters.title: The Contract
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. With the exposé public, the harbor board revotes and awards the route to the Hale line, with an investor offer attached—one contingent on a partner. Emeric slides the papers across the galley table and asks, not about money, but whether Xanthe is staying. Emotional beat: the question underneath every question.

chapters.title: Last Ferry of the Season
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. The final scheduled crossing of the year, lantern-lit, half the town aboard. At the dock, everyone assumes Xanthe is leaving; instead he signs the partnership papers on the wheelhouse chart table and kisses Emeric to a cheer from the deck. Emotional beat: arrival disguised as departure.

chapters.title: A Harbor for the Summer
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV, epilogue. Spring: the first ferry of the new season departs with Xanthe's published novel in the onboard bookshelf and his name on the partnership deed. He writes now in the morning, works the afternoon crossings, and mails letters that always arrive. Emotional beat: belonging, chosen daily, no longer borrowed.
